topic.name: Calculating the Intersection of Two Lines

question.text: Find the point of intersection of the lines $3x + 4y = 1$ and $2x - 2y = 3.$
question.explanation:
We need to solve the system of equations consisting of the two lines:

\[ \begin{cases} 3x + 4y = 1 \\ 2x - 2y = 3 \end{cases} \]

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $2,$ then we will get a $-4y$ term that can cancel with the $4y$ in the first equation:

\[ \begin{cases} 3x + 4y = 1 & \\ 2x - 2y = 3 & \Big| \: \times 2 \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 3x + 4y = 1 \\ 4x-4y= 6 \end{cases} \]

Adding the two equations eliminates the $y$-variable and allows us to solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ 3x + \cancel{4y} &= 1\\ 4x - \cancel{4y} &= 6 \\[5pt] \hline \left(3x+4x\right) &= \left(1+6\right)\\[5pt] 7x &= 7 \\[3pt] x &= 1 } \]

Finally, we can substitute $x=1$ into the equation $2x - 2y = 3$ to solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2x - 2y &= 3 \\[5pt] 2(1) - 2y &= 3 \\[5pt] 2 - 2y &= 3 \\[5pt] -2y &= 1 \\[5pt] y &= -\dfrac{1}{2} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=1, \, y=-\dfrac{1}{2}.$ So the coordinates of the point of intersection are $\left( 1, -\dfrac{1}{2} \right).$

example.title: Finding the Intersection of Two Lines Given in Standard Form

question.text: The lines $y = 3x-b$ and $y = x +5$ intersect at the point $C$ with coordinates $(a,2).$ Find the parameters $a$ and $b.$
question.explanation:
Since $(a,2)$ is the point of intersection of the two lines, the values $x=a, \, y=2$ must solve the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} y=3x-b \\ y=x+5 \end{cases} \]

We substitute $x=a, \, y=2$ to obtain a new system:

\[ \begin{cases} 2=3a-b \\ 2=a+5 \end{cases} \]

We can solve for $a$ in the second equation:

\begin{align*} 2 &= a+5 \\[3pt] -3 &= a \end{align*}

Then, we can substitute $a=-3$ into the first equation and solve for $b\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{align} 2&=3a-b \\[3pt] 2&=3(-3)-b \\[3pt] 2&=-9-b \\[3pt] 11&=-b \\[3pt] -11 &= b \end{align} \]

Therefore, $a = -3$ and $b = -11.$

example.title: Calculating Unknown Parameters Given a Point of Intersection

question.text: Find the point of intersection of the lines $2x + y = 12$ and $x - 2y = 6.$
question.explanation:
We need to solve the system of equations consisting of the two lines:

\[ \begin{cases} 2x + y = 12 \\ x - 2y = 6 \end{cases} \]

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $2,$ then we will get a $2y$ term that can cancel with the $-2y$ in the second equation:

\[ \begin{cases} 2x + y = 12 & \Big| \: \times 2 \\ x - 2y = 6 & \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 4x + 2y = 24 \\ x - 2y = 6 \end{cases} \]

Adding the two equations eliminates the $y$-variable and allows us to solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ 4x + \cancel{2y} &= 24\\ x - \cancel{2y} &= 6 \\[3pt] \hline (4x+x) &= (24+6)\\[3pt] 5x &= 30 \\[3pt] x &= 6 } \]

Finally, we can substitute $x=6$ into the equation $x - 2y = 6$ to solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} x - 2y &= 6 \\[3pt] 6-2y &= 6 \\[3pt] -2y&=0 \\[3pt] y&=0 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=6, \, y=0.$ So the coordinates of the point of intersection are $\left( 6, 0 \right).$
